title: All 15 scenarios passed
summary: All 15 Webots integration test scenarios passed (15/15, 100%). The PR scopes all persistent scene state by map_id, binding it to the mapping's named map. Changes include adding SCENE_MAP_ID env var, fixing Dockerfile wheel filenames, adding pymilvus dependency, forcing YOLO device, loading Milvus collections, partitioning scene-graph caches by map_id, and updating tests. The CI exercised builtin, cap, and flow scenarios covering file operations, plan control, camera/lidar snapshots, explore, mapping, memory, scene objects, speech, voiceprint, fault recovery, object navigation, and patrol observe.
pr_changes: Added SCENE_MAP_ID env var to manifest and map_id config to mapping service
Fixed Dockerfile to use canonical wheel filenames for torch/torchvision
Forced YOLO device to self._device in perception_concept_graphs.py
Added explicit load_collection call in persistence.py for milvus-lite 3.x
Partitioned SceneGraphStore caches by map_id in store.py
Computed map_id once in service.py and passed to ObjectStore and SceneGraphStore
Updated test_persistence.py to guard on milvus_lite import
test_result: 15 scenarios across builtin, cap, and flow families all passed. Builtin tests: fault_recovery_builtin, file_roundtrip, plan_control_builtins, run_command. Cap tests: camera_snapshot, explore_smoke, lidar_snapshot, mapping_save, memory_roundtrip, scene_object_fixture, speech_speak, voiceprint_list. Flow tests: fault_recovery, object_navigation, patrol_observe. All leaf calls succeeded as expected.
suggested_fix: No fix needed. Monitor for any regressions in scene object persistence across map boundaries in future runs.
risks_or_watchouts: Scene-graph cache partitioning by map_id may cause cold-start misses when switching maps
Milvus-lite 3.x explicit load_collection may add latency on first access
YOLO device forcing may affect performance on GPU-stable hosts
